specification.objective: Add safe compare, cherry-pick, and reset workflows to GitRex's existing commit context menu, with explicit targets, confirmations, conflict-aware feedback, and accurate repository refresh.

requirements.statement: Preserve Checkout Commit and Create Branch From Commit and add Compare, Cherry-pick, and Reset in the existing commit action menu.

Resolve the selected commit and a user-entered comparison reference to commit OIDs, then asynchronously display a bounded, scrollable changed-path/stat summary without changing refs, HEAD, index, worktree, or contacting remotes.

Cherry-pick the selected commit only onto an explicitly selected existing local branch; reject a dirty index/worktree before switching; review source and destination before mutation; and leave the destination active after success or conflict.

After cherry-pick success or any attempted cherry-pick that can alter repository state, refresh the snapshot; identify conflicts and provide continue/abort guidance without automatic recovery, and report refresh failure explicitly.

Offer typed Soft, Mixed, and Hard reset modes ordered with Soft selected by default; allow reset only when the displayed graph reference equals the current local branch and there are no unresolved conflicts.

Before reset, revalidate the expected current branch and HEAD OID in the worker; require explicit confirmation for each mode and a distinct additional destructive confirmation for Hard that shows branch, target, mode effects, and dirty-path information.
Run repository operations asynchronously; refresh the TUI after successful mutations and state-changing failures, while retaining the one-operation-at-a-time guard.
Pass references and branch names as direct Git argv data, use system Git, and add no implicit fetch, push, remote mutation, automatic stash, or automatic conflict resolution.
Update README and TUI help to describe comparison, cherry-pick destination and recovery behavior, reset effects, the Soft default, current-branch restriction, and Hard confirmation.

Add system-Git and TUI regressions for comparison immutability, cherry-pick success/dirty refusal/conflict refresh, all reset semantics and guards, confirmation/cancel paths, and long result navigation.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The existing commit menu retains its two actions and exposes Compare, Cherry-pick, and Reset with deterministic selection and cancellation behavior.
Comparison resolves commit-ish targets, reports equal or changed endpoints, remains bounded and navigable, and leaves repository state unchanged.

A clean cherry-pick applies the source to the selected local destination; dirty or invalid destinations fail before branch movement; a real conflict remains visible with refreshed status and recovery guidance.
Soft, Mixed, and Hard produce their distinct Git index/worktree effects; Soft is the initial mode; expected branch or HEAD mismatch aborts before reset.
Remote, detached, non-current graph, and unresolved-conflict contexts cannot enter reset; every reset needs review and Hard requires its extra destructive confirmation.
Successful mutations and state-changing failures refresh repository state; a failed refresh is explicit; no second operation can start while one is active.
README and help copy match tested behavior and explain consequences and recovery.
The existing policy's full tests, Clippy, and at-least-90-percent line coverage pass, alongside formatting and cross-platform CI.

invariants: Selected commit identity is captured when its action flow begins.
Comparison never mutates repository state or contacts a remote.
Cherry-pick destination is an existing local branch explicitly shown before operation; dirty preflight occurs before switching.
Cherry-pick conflict state is left for the user and reflected in a refreshed snapshot when possible.
Reset target is a resolved commit OID; expected current branch and HEAD are rechecked immediately before mutation.
Reset operates only on the current local branch represented by the displayed graph; detached and remote refs cannot authorize it.
Soft is the default mode; Hard has a separate explicit confirmation boundary.
Git receives references and names through direct argv, never shell interpolation.
No implicit fetch, push, stash, force-push, conflict recovery, or unrelated branch-workflow behavior is introduced.
forbidden_states: A comparison target is executed without successful commit resolution.
A dirty cherry-pick request switches away from the current branch.
A cherry-pick conflict is reported as state-preserving without refreshing or warning about refresh failure.
A displayed non-current, remote, or detached graph ref can reset the current branch.
A reset proceeds after its expected branch or HEAD changes.
Hard reset executes after only the ordinary reset confirmation.
A conflict is automatically continued, aborted, stashed, or resolved.
inputs: Selected commit OID from the graph history.
Selected typed reset mode, resolved target OID, expected current branch, and expected HEAD OID.
outputs: Bounded, scrollable comparison summary with endpoint identity.
Cherry-pick success or conflict feedback, recovery guidance, and refreshed repository snapshot when available.
Reset mode, target, previous/resulting HEAD feedback, and refreshed repository snapshot when available.

failure_semantics.statement: An invalid comparison reference, source commit, or local destination fails before the associated comparison or branch switch.
A dirty cherry-pick preflight refuses before switching branches; a failed attempted cherry-pick refreshes repository state and reports conflict/recovery details when present.
Reset refuses before mutation when detached, on a different branch/HEAD than expected, on an unresolved conflict, or when the displayed graph is not the current local branch.
If a repository mutation is attempted but a subsequent snapshot refresh fails, preserve the mutation result and tell the user to refresh manually.
Esc at any input, selection, or confirmation phase cancels without starting the corresponding Git mutation.

transitions: Commit menu -> Compare target input -> asynchronous result -> scroll/close.
Commit menu -> Cherry-pick local branch selection -> source/destination review -> operation -> refreshed success/conflict result.
Commit menu -> Reset mode picker (Soft default) -> ordinary confirmation -> Hard-only destructive confirmation -> operation -> refreshed result.
Esc cancels the current phase and returns to the previous safe phase without starting a mutation.
revalidation: Resolve source and target refs to commit OIDs in GitClient.
Before cherry-pick, require clean status and validate an exact existing local destination.
Before reset, compare actual symbolic local branch and HEAD OID with the confirmed expected values.

components: TUI Commit Actions state, rendering, and keyboard controller
Asynchronous operation request, execution, outcome, and snapshot refresh
interfaces: CommitAction menu variants and action flow transitions
Typed Git reset mode and GitClient compare/cherry-pick/reset methods
compatibility: No CLI command or output changes.
Existing checkout-commit and create-branch-from-commit semantics remain.
System Git remains the runtime backend; no persistent schema changes.
